title: Run the optional Mermaid and MathJax renderers on Windows
lead:
Third child of s13. Covers `--with-mermaid` and `--with-math` setup and their
build-time renderers on Windows.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
On Windows, npm is `npm.cmd`, and Puppeteer's Chromium and the locked runtimes
resolve paths differently. Without this slice, a Windows user either cannot
install the optional renderers or gets failures at build time. Keep this
separate from s22 and s23 so the core Windows path can land first.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
install.py (require_node, ensure_mermaid, ensure_math: the npm and node
invocations), quire_mermaid.py and quire_math.py (the renderer startup and
manifest paths), mermaid-render.mjs and mathjax-render.mjs (only where a POSIX
path or file URL is assumed), test_render.py, README.md (optional renderer
notes).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
With `os.name` patched to "nt":

- The installer calls npm through the path that `shutil.which("npm")` resolves,
  which is `npm.cmd`, with no `shell=True`. Node's version check is unchanged.
- Each renderer finds its locked runtime manifest under the checkout using
  Windows paths.
- The Node workers receive paths they can turn into file URLs. Test this with
  `pathToFileURL` in the .mjs files, or with a Python-side test of the argument
  they receive.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
- Use the resolved `npm.cmd` path directly. Python's `subprocess` runs `.cmd`
  files through cmd.exe, and its argument quoting is safe for these fixed
  arguments. Do not add `shell=True`.
- Audit both .mjs workers for `'/'` path joins and bare `file://` string
  building, and use `node:path` and `pathToFileURL` throughout.
- No new dependencies and no network at build time. Setup stays behind the
  explicit `--with-mermaid` and `--with-math` options.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: python3 test_quire.py; black --check quire.py test_quire.py; flake8 quire.py test_quire.py. A real Windows run of test_render_integration.py is needed for acceptance; report it as unverified if no Windows host is available.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Do not commit; orchestrator handles it.
